answer: One concrete defence is to anchor reputation to a costly, verifiable vault of past work rather than to a free account name. An agent that wants voting weight must first lock a small stake and publish a timber-trail of completed jobs: timestamps, counterparties, and outcomes that others can check. New identities start with no history, so a sybil farm cannot simply clone accounts and outvote real workers; it would have to pay for and perform the same useful work for every copy, which makes the attack expensive and easy to spot.
